note: Cayman Islands, read in Workforce Opportunities and Residency Cayman's application form T1 for a Temporary Work Permit (revised August 2026) and its Work Permit & Permanent Residency FAQ (my.egov.ky/web/worc) on 2026-10-30. A Temporary Work Permit is addressed to the Director of WORC, the employee and the employer (or the self-employed) completing its two parts (work for the sponsor); it is asked for one, three or six months (eight for seasonal work only; six kept); a musical or theatrical entertainer adds a demo of the show and an event its advertising. Its fee is the work permit fee for the occupation (not on the form) plus a non-refundable application fee of CI$150 to CI$500 by the annual fee's size, so no single fee is kept; where the worker must be isn't stated ('either'). Annual work permits, permanent residence (which carries an annual payment) and its years aren't on the pages read; the right to be Caymanian asks fifteen years' legal and ordinary residence (Immigration law, as the FAQ quotes it).

sources.title: WORC, Application for a Temporary Work Permit (form T1, revised August 2026)
sources.said: THE APPLICATION FOR THE GRANT OF A TEMPORARY WORK PERMIT SHOULD BE ADDRESSED TO: ... The first part is to be completed by the employee and the second part by the employer or the self-employed. ... How long do you wish this Temporary Work Permit to be valid for: 1 Month 3 Months 6 Months 8 Months (Seasonal Temporary Only) ... CI $150 (where the annual work permit fee is $2,100 or less); ... CI $500 (where the annual work permit fee is more than $10,400) ... Musical and Theatric Entertainer: Provide a demo tape/CD/DVD of show

sources.title: WORC, Work Permit & Permanent Residency FAQ
sources.said: Annual PR payments can be paid in person at the WORC Apollo House West office. ... if the person has been legally and ordinarily resident in the Islands for at least fifteen years
